title: Lab size, from everyone alone to one lab of everyone, on a graph where every level is equally hard
html:
Lab size, from everyone alone to one lab of everyone, on a graph where every level is equally hard

Question: On a graph where every level is equally hard, with 24 agents in labs of 1 to 24 that share inside the lab, how much money does the field need, against OSO across the whole field?

Answer: At budgets 8–16: best Traditional (α = 1, β = 0), alone (7 measures). At budget 32: best OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money and waste; no clear difference on targets solved, bounty value, ROI and money to the main level. At budget 64: best OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money and waste; no clear difference on money to the main level. At budgets 128–256: best Labs of 24 (one lab of everyone). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level and waste. At budgets 512–2048: best Labs of 24 (one lab of everyone). Against traditional, clearly better on ROI, knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level and waste; no clear difference on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value and knowledge found (bits). At budgets 4096–65536: best Labs of 24 (one lab of everyone). Against traditional, clearly better on ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level and waste; no clear difference on hardest level, targets solved and bounty value. (Compared at each budget; 8 measures, a clear difference is more than 2.7 standard errors.)
